subject: OrionMed on-prem: sustained throughput drop & 5xx spike — remediation playbook request
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@orionmed.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@orionmed.com, claire.dunn@orionmed.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop / 5xx cascade on our on‑prem cluster

Rafael —

We just saw a sustained throughput drop across our on‑prem VPC cluster (orionmed‑prod) starting ~08:45 PDT. P95 increased from ~210ms to >2.5s and we're seeing a 6–8% 5xx rate for user requests. The batch/async pipelines are also piling up; we've stopped a downstream job as a precaution.

I've attached the trace dump and KV cache stats. The cluster team is seeing steady GPU utilization but large queuing at the front end.

This is impacting triage and care flows. Can Redwood triage immediately and provide an on‑call escalation path / temporary rollback to a conservative config? We need a mitigation plan within the hour.

—Rajiv
Platform Ops | OrionMed

Attachments: orionmed-slowtrace-20270511.txt, orionmed-kvcache-stats-20270511.csv

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@orionmed.com>, Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@orionmed.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:24 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop / 5xx cascade on our on‑prem cluster

Rajiv —

Thanks for the data. I'm pulling the traces now. First pass: looks like large queueing at the private ingress layer (proxy) and growing KV cache miss amplification on hot prefixes. Dropped requests are hitting our fallback into the larger model (decoder path) causing CPU/GPU backpressure even though GPU % looks normal.

Immediate asks:
- Can your ops pause non‑urgent async batches and reduce burst workers for the next 30m?
- Confirm whether any config changes were pushed at ~08:30 (autoscaler, nginx/proxy, or model variant toggles).

I'm escalating to Laura (private infra lead) and Marissa (SRE). We'll propose a conservative playbook: 1) pin model variant to the lower memory/decoder variant, 2) lower max concurrency on the frontend proxy, 3) enable aggressive prefix K/V cache warming for the hot keys, 4) temporary traffic throttling on non‑critical routes.

Onstandby — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Lead, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

Attachments: remediation-runbook-v2.pdf

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: claire.dunn@orionmed.com, rajiv.menon@orionmed.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:22:10 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sudden throughput drop / 5xx cascade on our on‑prem cluster

Team —

Looping you in. Rafael's summary matches the short telemetry I pulled. Priorities: stop customer impact (latency/5xx), then root cause. Quick plan (30m cadence):

1) Throttle non‑essential traffic (Auth/reporting endpoints) — Claire/Rajiv to confirm routes we can deprioritize.
2) Pin model variant to quantized v1b (lower mem footprint) — Jonas to run CI smoke and push config.
3) Reduce frontend max concurrency to 12 per proxy worker.
4) Backfill prefix cache for identified hot keys (Rafael / Orion infra).
5) If p95 doesn't recover in 45m, activate fallback to hosted infer (route <5% of traffic) as graceful degradation.

Marissa — please coordinate the runbook execution and update OPS‑3427. We need a short exec note for Orion leadership in ~60–90 minutes.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Dir, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: rajiv.menon@orionmed.com, claire.dunn@orionmed.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:31:54 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden throughput drop / 5xx cascade on our on‑prem cluster

On it. Execution plan (I will run these in this order and update every 15m):

A) Apply proxy concurrency cap (12) via remote config; monitor queue depth (expected effect in ~2–3m).
B) Trigger variant pin to quantized v1b (Jonas to validate readiness).
C) Start a targeted cache backfill job for the top 50 hot prefixes from the attached trace — Rafael please confirm keys.
D) If we still see >3% 5xx after steps A–C, start traffic siphon to hosted fallback (rate limited, tokenized).

I'll attach logs and short diffs to OPS‑3427. Rafael — please send the hot key list and confirm if Orion can throttle async workers.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Lead SRE, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@orionmed.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: claire.dunn@orionmed.com, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:44:18 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden throughput drop / 5xx cascade on our on‑prem cluster

Marissa / Rafael —

We paused async workers, turned off a non‑critical telemetry stream, and confirmed no config pushes at 08:30. Hot key list below (first 8 of 50):
- patient:summary:most_recent
- encounter:notes:hot
- lab:result:cache_hot
- imaging:thumbnail:patient_hot
- meds:list:active
- orders:queue:hot
- billing:account:search
- auth:session:hot

We're ready for the config pins and proxy cap. If you want, we can open a direct line (hangouts) for playbook coordination.

—Rajiv

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: rajiv.menon@orionmed.com, claire.dunn@orionmed.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: OrionMed — executive note & post‑mortem request

Team / Orion leadership —

Quick executive summary for OrionMed leadership: on 11 May we observed a spike in p95 latency and a 5xx rate correlated with KV cache miss amplification on hot prefixes and proxy queueing. Immediate mitigations (concurrency cap, model variant pin, targeted prefix backfill) restored service levels to p95 < 350ms and reduced 5xxs to <0.5% within ~28 minutes. Traffic bypass to hosted fallback was prepared but not required.

Root cause hypothesis: a combination of a transient change in traffic distribution (hot key amplification) plus insufficient early cache warming for prioritized prefixes after a short cold window. Secondary contributing factor: aggressive frontend concurrency defaults in the customer's proxy config that allowed request bursts to queue and amplify decoder load.

Open asks / next steps (owner):
- Run full post‑mortem with Orion infra and Redwood SREs (Marissa / Orion platform) — due 2027‑05‑18.
- Add prioritized prefix warming in our private deploy templates (Jonas) — due 2027‑05‑25.
- Consider safe default concurrency throttle in our on‑prem quickstart (Laura) — draft by 2027‑05‑20.
- Provide a short rolling‑upgrade knob to auto‑pin variants on performance regressions (Rafael / Eng) — proposal by 2027‑06‑01.

I'll compile a 1‑page note for Orion's CEO and our CRO. Rafael — please attach the runbook + traces (done). Marissa — please push the OPS‑3427 update with logs.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Dir, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
